title: Tailwind TTFT Stabilizer: cross-variant latency surge and emergency hotfix
creator: Amina Patel
description:
Summary: Starting 2025-02-17 22:10 UTC we observed a sustained TTFT (time-to-first-token) increase and tokens/sec drop affecting a subset of long-context generation requests across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Impacted traffic corresponded primarily to quantized model variants (int8) and mixed fanout patterns from chat and batch endpoints. Several enterprise customers reported elevated p50/p95 first-byte latency and CPU/GPU utilization spikes on host nodes. This ticket tracks triage, the emergency hotfix we pushed, and next steps for a durable fix.

Observed metrics: p50 TTFT increased by 150-400ms on average, p95 up to +1.2s on affected clusters; tokens/sec dropped ~22% for affected variants. Regression appeared correlated with a kernel selector heuristic change rolled out in runtime-1.20 on 2025-02-16.

Hypothesis: a recent kernel-autoselect heuristic favored an int8 kernel path when a mixed-precision weight shard was present; at certain sequence lengths the kernel caused increased micro-batch handshake latency and KV warmup thrash under multi-tenant fanout. The scheduler then amplified latency by reordering small requests behind stalled streams.

Why this ticket is different: this is cross-deployment (hosted/dedicated/private) and cross-variant regression tied to the new kernel routing heuristic. Impact requires coordinated mitigation across control plane routing, runtime kernel flags, and customer communications.
reproduction_steps: Start a multi-tenant fanout workload using model v2-int8 and v2-fp16 variants with interleaved short and long sequences (priming + 1024 tokens).
Target ~150 concurrent sessions across a dedicated pool or hosted region with mixture of streaming and non-streaming requests.
Observe first-token latency and tokens/sec for int8 variant versus fp16; repro shows increased handshake latency after runtime-1.20 kernel-selector is enabled.
Toggle kernel_autoselect=false in runtime config to confirm regression goes away.
mitigation: 2025-02-18 01:40 UTC: emergency hotfix deployed to revert kernel-selector heuristic (feature flag: kernel_autoselect=false) across affected clusters.
Activated temporary router rule to prefer fp16 variants for mixed fanout sessions for critical enterprise customers (customers list in linked_docs).
Increased KV cache retention for warm sessions from 60s -> 180s for targeted pools to reduce warmup churn.
Customer-facing communication drafted and sent to escalations channel; on-call PM engaged for bridge calls.
resolution: Hotfix deployed and rolled out incrementally to hosted and dedicated pools; initial telemetry shows p50 TTFT back to baseline for most customers (monitored window 30m-2h).
Private deployments: provided patch notes and a toggle to ops contacts; several customers applied the kernel_autoselect=false flag manually and confirmed improvement.
Root-cause investigation continues; durable fix requires adjusted heuristic and scheduler safeguards (see next_steps).
next_steps: Engineer: implement conservative kernel selection thresholds that consider sequence-length distribution and recent KV hit-rate before picking int8 path (owner: @cnguyen).
SRE: run a controlled soak test for candidate heuristic on canary pools for 48h (owner: @maria-chen).
Product: update model catalog entries to mark risky mixed-precision variants with advisory notes (owner: @ethan-brooks).
Deliverable: runtime-1.20.1 with heuristic fix + scheduler preemption guard; plan for rollout window and rollback criteria.
comments: 2025-02-18 02:05 UTC - Amina Patel: Noticed correlation with kernel selection flip. Kernel flag revert helped in dev cluster. Eng+SRE to coordinate rollback across regions.
2025-02-18 03:12 UTC - Carlos Nguyen: Reverted flag in us-west and eu-west canaries; immediate improvement observed. Deploying to remaining pools in waves.
2025-02-18 05:40 UTC - Maria Chen: KV retention bump mitigated some oscillation but does not fully address scheduler reorder; added to next_steps.
2025-02-19 11:00 UTC - Support Ops: Two enterprise customers (AcmeCorp, FinSys) reported restored performance after flag applied; collecting long-tail telemetry for 72h.

customer_list_affected: several mid-market customers - anonymized list in linked_docs
postmortem_plan: Complete RCA within 7 days, include timeline, metrics, and backfill tests in CI to detect kernel-scheduler regressions. Add automated canary that validates TTFT and tokens/sec for representative mixed-precision fanout patterns before any kernel selector release.
notes: Avoid reintroducing kernel_autoselect heuristic without a scheduler safeguard. Consider adding a per-deployment override in Console to let customers opt-in to experimental kernels.
